key_insight: A physics-aligned simulator (SIM1) can generate large, realistic zero-shot training data for deformable-object manipulation, enabling policies trained purely in simulation to transfer to real-world cloth and soft-object tasks.
problem_solved: Addresses the data scarcity and sim-to-real gap for deformable-object robotics by overcoming rigid-body–based simulators that produce mismatched geometry, unstable soft dynamics, and unsuitable motion primitives for cloth-like interactions.
method: Design a simulator that explicitly models deformable physics: accurate contact, topology changes, and shape evolution to produce realistic soft-body behavior.
Use the simulator as a zero-shot data scaler: generate diverse, physics-consistent manipulation trajectories and state observations at scale for policy training without real-world fine-tuning.
Incorporate motion primitives and interaction priors tailored to deformables (e.g., grasping, folding, sliding) to produce realistic demonstrations and robust policies.
impact: Reduces reliance on costly real-world data collection and domain adaptation, enabling faster development and deployment of robust deformable-object manipulation policies for robotics and embodied AI.
visual_elements: Side-by-side comparison: simulated cloth vs. real cloth responding to the same manipulation (visual realism & dynamics match).
Pipeline diagram: SIM1 simulator -> large synthetic dataset -> policy training -> zero-shot deployment on real robot.
Bar/line chart: success rates or task performance (sim-only vs. rigid-sim baseline vs. real-world) showing transfer gains.
Iconic schematic: physics-alignment components (contact, topology, shape) highlighting what the simulator models differently.
paper_title: SIM1: Physics-Aligned Simulator as Zero-Shot Data Scaler in Deformable Worlds
paper_authors: Yunsong Zhou, Hangxu Liu, Xuekun Jiang, Xing Shen, Yuanzhen Zhou
